message: docs: reconcile status authoring, current regression scope and review guidance

edits:
`onActivate` and `onDeactivate` optionally emit a `stateChanged` event with an explicit target and narration template. The supported bindings are `subject`, `source` and `actionTarget`, using the shared [name-template grammar](entity-names.md#authored-narration-templates): bare `.name` or an explicit `:indefinite`/`:definite` article. World-authored templates choose the wording; the engine does not infer a mechanic from a name. Committed events use the existing observation audience, experience and conversation boundaries. They are narration, never speech or accepted model responses. Temporary perception restriction does not itself declare a participant physically out of conversation range; ordinary distance/inactivity rules still apply.
The creator-only `POST /api/god/status-effects` accepts `{}` to inspect the registry, or `{policy, expectedRevision}` to replace it. Admission validates every operator, field, attribute and definition reference before committing. It rejects stale revisions and unknown fields, and removal of an effect still required by installed body or cognition policy. An explicitly null dream policy has no effect dependency. Changed/removed native singleton definitions deactivate their existing instances under the old definition before replacement; unchanged definitions retain their episodes. Retained independent contributions instead require their exact old definition and reject unsupported replacement/removal. The [reviewed World Agent write path](world-agent-runtime.md#durable-write-sessions) already calls this same boundary through its `status-effect-policy` adapter, with exact draft approval and Apply receipts. A dedicated direct settings form remains a separate UI extension, not a missing policy mutation mechanism. Broad non-actor attribute authoring remains unimplemented; the existing reviewed attribute-binding/value adapters operate on supported actor bodies.

- [ ] **SR12 — Native participant roster:** compare outcomes, event order and saved RNG with live full enumeration at matched admitted elapsed-time boundaries for mixed inert objects, actors, animals and heat sources. Include death/incapacity, cooling fires, landing, long native actions, queued plan commands replacing a draft, memory-disabled populations and memory capability changes between advances. Do not retain revoked draft entities. When a future native family adds/removes participants or relevant components, its mutation must refresh the roster before the affected phase; add that regression with the family. Roster reuse does not justify coalescing application-level perception/commit boundaries.
- [ ] Qualify status-policy edits through the delivered reviewed World Agent adapter and existing creator API; both call the native registry owner. A dedicated direct settings form and broad non-actor attribute authoring remain extensions under [EWF](extensible-world-foundation.md) and [WW](world-agent-writes.md), not a second policy editor or mutation owner. Extend target selectors, area effects, general stacking or conserved transfers only for a concrete mechanic. The delivered [independent capability contributions](../status-effects.md#independent-capability-contributions) already combine admitted sources on a subject; do not rebuild them or infer general rate/stacking support from that finite family.
These deferred automated cases span delivered family authoring and the read-only promise list, plus the still-proposed promise-management and feeling-process controls. Their current scope and native/manual evidence remain in the focused trackers; a documentation review does not run or satisfy these cases. Do not author/run suites without the applicable task authorization.
- [x] Preserve a character's own promise attribution through stored memory and `## My commitments`: personal wording receives the native speaker identity and keeps self/recognized/unknown speakers distinct. [PW01 branch evidence](../verification/level1-decisions.md#pw01-reliability-repairs--october-2-2026) covers native memory and the real director context fixture. [BW22](base-world.md#bw22--observer-safe-names-in-event-text) subsequently repaired targeted-event name disclosure with native and PostgreSQL evidence; broader automated/browser acceptance remains separate.

Apply [experience-led prioritization](../openlegend-prioritize/SKILL.md) when the review changes selection or priority. Check the intended player experience across the whole game, not just the subsystem under review. OpenLegend needs a complete playable, enjoyable loop before optional simulation detail or architectural novelty. Separate player value from implementation effort and dependency order: a cheap maintenance action is not automatically important, while enemies, controls, combat, exploration, rewards, progression and recovery cannot be demoted merely because they require unfamiliar work. Preserve approved scope and correctness constraints, but retire superseded “next milestone” claims. When an accepted priority revision is maintained on another branch, identify that owner and integration boundary rather than silently merging its files, duplicating its ranking system or treating old local scores as current.

Apply [purpose-based validation](../../../AGENTS.md#validate-only-for-a-concrete-purpose) when reviewing rejecting checks or proposing new ones: identify the consumer, realistic invalid input and concrete harm. Do not retain obsolete score-normalization assertions or duplicate trusted-boundary validation just because a historical checklist requested them. This does not weaken authority, privacy, accounting or current-format integrity.
